english: Let $a$ be a positive real number and let $f:[1,2]\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x+\dfrac{a}{x}$. If the least value of $f$ is $\dfrac{9}{5}$, then the value of $a$ is ______.
hindi: माना $a$ एक धनात्मक वास्तविक संख्या है तथा $f:[1,2]\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x+\dfrac{a}{x}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। यदि $f$ का न्यूनतम मान $\dfrac{9}{5}$ है, तो $a$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f$ is continuous on the closed interval $[1,2]$, so it is bounded and attains its least value, at $x=1$, $x=2$ or at the critical point $x=\sqrt a$ ($f'(x)=1-\dfrac{a}{x^{2}}$)
Case $1\le a\le4$ ($\sqrt a\in[1,2]$): least value $2\sqrt a\ge2>\dfrac95$, impossible (the AM-GM answer $a=\dfrac{81}{100}$ has $\sqrt a=\dfrac{9}{10}\notin[1,2]$)
Case $a>4$: $f'<0$ on $[1,2]$, least value $f(2)=2+\dfrac a2>4$, impossible
solution_full: $f$ is continuous on the closed, bounded interval $[1,2]$, so it is bounded there and attains a greatest and a least value. The least value occurs at an end point $x=1$, $x=2$ or at an interior critical point.

$f'(x)=1-\dfrac{a}{x^{2}}$ vanishes only at $x=\sqrt a$ (as $x>0$), and $f'$ changes from negative to positive there, so $x=\sqrt a$ is a minimum point of $f$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $f(\sqrt a)=2\sqrt a$.

Case $1\le a\le4$: $\sqrt a\in[1,2]$, so the least value of $f$ on $[1,2]$ is $2\sqrt a\ge2$. It cannot equal $\dfrac95<2$. (Setting $2\sqrt a=\dfrac95$ gives $a=\dfrac{81}{100}$, but then $\sqrt a=\dfrac9{10}$ lies outside $[1,2]$, so this value is wrong.)
Case $a>4$: $\sqrt a>2$, $f'(x)<0$ on $[1,2]$, $f$ is decreasing, and the least value is $f(2)=2+\dfrac a2>4$. Impossible.
Case $0<a<1$: $\sqrt a<1$, $f'(x)>0$ on $[1,2]$, $f$ is increasing, and the least value is $f(1)=1+a$. Then $1+a=\dfrac95$ gives $a=\dfrac45$, which indeed lies in $(0,1)$.
Check: for $a=\dfrac45$, $f(1)=\dfrac95$, $f(2)=\dfrac{12}{5}$ and $f$ is increasing on $[1,2]$, so the least value is $\dfrac95$.
originality_note: New: an inverse problem (the least value on a closed interval is given, the parameter is asked) in which the AM-GM critical value 2 sqrt(a) gives a tempting wrong answer 0.81 because the critical point falls outside the interval (way 5, link of interval extremum with the location of the critical point). Closest known: least value of x + a/x for x > 0, which is 2 sqrt(a). Different because: the student must split on the position of sqrt(a) relative to [1, 2], and only the end-point case is consistent.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, function and domain introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy/numpy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that the least value of f on [1,2] is strictly increasing in a, so a = 4/5 is the only solution (numerical scan over a in (0, 5]). Changed: No change.
key_step: Case split on the position of the critical point sqrt(a) relative to [1, 2]; the interior case gives 2 sqrt(a) >= 2 > 9/5, so the minimum is at the end point x = 1.
justification: Two linked ideas: the extreme value on a closed interval (end points vs interior critical point) and the consistency check of the case, with a strong trap (a = 0.81) and no options. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q1 (L3), extrema decided by a sign analysis of f'.

concept_use.Bounded functions; greatest and least va: f is continuous on the closed interval [1,2], hence bounded with attained least value; the cases a in [1,4] and a > 4 give least values >= 2 and > 4, so they are rejected.
concept_use.Greatest and least value of a function i: Least value on [1,2] found by comparing the end points with the critical point x = sqrt(a); for 0 < a < 1 it is f(1) = 1 + a = 9/5.
